head: 3eeae7ebfdf2ab862d368fc22a8025ec69f83170
classification_reasons: Spec is tight: both of spec.md's Flagged concerns are closed with concrete, panel-recorded decisions (empty input raises ValueError('mean() requires at least one value') from a guard clause mean owns; parameter type is Sequence[float]), and every other section (Requirements, Design, Open questions from intent, Acceptance) now states those same decisions consistently rather than the mixed 'still open' wording the prior HEAD had, so acceptance for every case (normal, single-element, empty) is a single measurable assertion.

Blast radius is small: the diff touches only changes/0002-add-mean-helper-to-sample-pkg/{spec.md,plan.md,status.yaml,evidence/**}; the code files plan.md names for phase (c) (sample_pkg/calc.py, sample_pkg/__init__.py, tests/test_calc.py) are not yet touched, none is on sdlc.yaml's risk_list, none is a guardrail file.

Coverage is the criterion that keeps this non-routine: mean is a brand-new function with no existing test exercising it today; the three tests that will cover it (test_mean, test_mean_single_element, test_mean_empty) are written in this same change, not pre-existing, so 'code the existing tests already cover' does not hold. All three routine conditions must hold for routine; this one does not.
attempted: Intent: re-checked intent.md's Proposed outcome bullet 5 (spec closes flagged concerns as 'decided (by panel): ...', evidence/ carries decisions-b.md and panel/ files) against the current spec.md and evidence/. Both flagged-concern bullets begin with 'decided (by panel): ...' with no duplicated prefix and no leftover 'is undecided' fragment; decisions-b.json/.md and evidence/panel/b-1-*, b-2-*, b-items.json all exist and agree with each other and with spec.md's final wording. The gap that caused the earlier escalate (missing panel evidence) and the cosmetic bug flagged in the prior continue verdict (duplicated 'decided (by panel): decided (by panel): ...' prefix on concern 2, and Requirements/Design/Open questions/Acceptance still saying 'not decided' after Flagged concerns had already closed the items) are both gone: I read the current Requirements, Design, Open questions from intent, Flagged concerns and Acceptance sections end to end and every one of them now states the same two decisions (Sequence[float]; explicit ValueError guard) consistently, in past tense where appropriate ('was undecided going into the panel round', 'answered by the deferred-review panel').

Spec and plan: plan.md's step 1 code block (guard clause raising ValueError, divide(sum(values), len(values)) otherwise, Sequence[float] signature) matches spec.md's Design section exactly; plan.md's Files/Order/Risks/Options-not-taken/Proof sections are internally consistent and correctly attribute the rejected ZeroDivisionError-propagation and Iterable[float] alternatives to the panel round, matching decisions-b.json items 1 and 2. plan.md itself was not touched by the latest (tidy) commit and did not need to be: it already carried the final decided signature and body from the panel-decision commit.

Proof: compared decisions-b.json/.md and evidence/panel/b-1-*, b-2-* (reviewer, devil's advocate, conciliator, one round each) against sample_pkg/calc.py's actual current code (not read into context beyond confirming divide's and percent's signatures already cited by spec.md/plan.md): the panel's factual claims about existing precedent are consistent with what spec.md/plan.md describe elsewhere in the repo. evidence/panel/b-items.json now shows decided: 2, pending: [], gate: wait, iterations.used: 2 of cap 2 — consistent with status.yaml's iterations: 2 and with both concerns being closed; no stale bookkeeping remains at this HEAD.

Blast radius: no sample_pkg/*.py, tests/*.py, .claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md or sdlc.yaml is touched by this diff; confirmed against sdlc.yaml's risk_list (auth, data migrations, money movement, production config) directly and none applies.

Policies: re-read spec.md's per-skill applicability calls (security-baseline, ux-conventions, data-conventions correctly n/a for a pure in-process arithmetic helper) and the coding-standards rules (rule 2 match-surrounding-code, rule 5 no unnecessary dependency) the panel actually leaned on for both decisions in b-1-reviewer.md/b-2-reviewer.md and the conciliator jsons — reasoning is specific to this codebase (divide/percent precedent), not generic boilerplate, and matches what spec.md now states.

Tests: no test files are touched in this phase-(b) diff, consistent with design-only scope; plan.md pins test_mean_empty to pytest.raises(ValueError) around mean([]), which pins mean's own guard clause rather than a coincidental ZeroDivisionError from divide — directly addressing the devil's advocate's point in b-1-advocate.md that a bare ZeroDivisionError-via-divide test would pass with the wrong implementation (e.g. divide(len(values), sum(values)) or divide(0,0)).
